clue.text: Changes to incomes are his responsibility

definitions.text: Changes to incomes are his responsibility

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the following two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about who is to blame when people's pay alters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' rearranges TO and INCOMES; the whole clue then describes the answer, since shifts in earnings are what this professional studies.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in the study of money, wages and markets is answerable for advice on shifts in earnings.

clue.text: Far from friendly at 100 years of age!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
someone of many years of age is old

explanation.surface: A centenarian being described as rather unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilly, unwelcoming manner is the opposite of friendly.

clue.text: Nicked when seen around the church

indicators.note: around tells us the word for seen goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: something seen has been noted
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone stole something while being watched near a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an edge with a small cut or groove made in it.

clue.text: African animal that sounds like just any domestic pet

indicators.note: sounds like says the phrase is spoken and the answer is spelt differently

parts.note: just any means mere, and a common domestic pet is a cat

explanation.surface: Comparing an exotic creature with an ordinary household pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small burrowing mongoose of southern Africa, famous for standing upright on watch.

clue.text: Pace at which tame animals return

indicators.note: return in a down clue means the word for tame animals is read backwards

parts.note: tame animals kept at home are pets

explanation.surface: How fast domesticated creatures come back home.
explanation.definitionFit: A single stride is one pace.

clue.text: Lass performs with diplomacy-but only intermittently

indicators.note: performs suggests the letters of lass and diplomacy go through their paces into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman acts tactfully, but not consistently.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in fits and starts happens only now and then.

clue.text: Given a number

parts.note: number reads as one more numb: someone given a numbing drug before surgery, not a figure

explanation.definitionFit: A patient put under with a drug is made numb, rendered insensible to pain.

clue.text: Confess to knocking over a jar of coffee

definitions.text: knocking over a jar of coffee

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to an accident in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means reveal a secret; literally it is upsetting a container of coffee beans.

clue.text: Doctor cooks spinach with extremes of incompetency!

indicators.note: cooks suggests the letters are mixed up as if prepared in a kitchen

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremes of picks the first and last letters of incompetency

explanation.surface: A doctor who is a hopeless cook prepares some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' gives I and Y from 'incompetency', and 'cooks' mixes them with SPINACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical practitioner is a doctor.

clue.text: One thousand intercede straight away

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to intercede between parties is to mediate

explanation.surface: A huge number of people step in at once to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at once, without delay, happens instantly.

clue.text: He might entertain a large crowd

explanation.surface: A man throwing a big party for many guests.
explanation.definitionFit: One who receives guests at a party; also a great multitude, as in a host of people.

clue.text: Point to the fish with trembling hand

parts.note: S, for south, is a point of the compass
hake is a sea fish related to cod

explanation.surface: Someone nervously pointing at a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor or quiver of the hand is a shaking movement.

clue.text: Side of fresh meat

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of meat are made anew in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A joint of meat, newly cut.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a side is a group of players.

clue.text: Starting salary of trainee in the mine caused division

indicators.note: starting means just the first letter of salary
in tells us the trainee's letter goes inside the word for mine

parts.note: a mine is a pit
L stands for learner, a trainee driver

explanation.surface: A dispute over a learner miner's first wage.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on a trainee driver's car in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something, past tense, is to have broken it into parts.

clue.text: Forming ideas about bacteria perhaps

explanation.surface: Theorising about microbes.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds or beginnings of a thought; also microbes, of which bacteria are one kind.

clue.text: Ran round to return the saucepan-and stayed

indicators.note: round says the word for ran goes all round the cooking vessel

parts.note: to have run fast is to have sped

indicators.note: to return means the word for saucepan is read backwards

parts.note: a saucepan is a pot

explanation.surface: Someone dashes back to fetch the saucepan, then stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' is a verb here supplying a synonym, not the definition; 'to return' turns the pot into TOP before 'round' wraps the speed word about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stopped is to have stayed, as in stopped at a friend's.

clue.text: Put letters in-in support

indicators.note: put suggests the letters are placed in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A request to slot correspondence into some kind of holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame with legs used to hold up a tabletop is a kind of support.

clue.text: Upper limit of the roof

explanation.surface: The highest point a building reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap on prices is a ceiling; also the overhead surface of a room.

clue.text: Information on Eric, a member of the species

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
taken as written

explanation.surface: Data about a man named Eric, one example of his kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic describes what is typical of a whole class or kind rather than one individual.

clue.text: Sanctimonious poem I wrote about a buried city

indicators.note: about says the word for sanctimonious goes around the rest

parts.note: pi is British slang for sanctimonious, short for pious

indicators.note: wrote suggests the letters of poem I are composed afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-righteous poet composing verse about a lost city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanctimonious' looks like a description of the poet but gives British slang PI; 'wrote' jumbles POEM I into OMPEI, which sits 'about'-wise inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town near Naples was buried in ash when Vesuvius erupted in AD 79.

clue.text: Position for a gentleman of letters

definitions.text: Position for a gentleman of letters

parts.note: a post is a job or position
a gentleman is a man

explanation.surface: Seeking a job suitable for a literary man.
explanation.walkthrough: A man of letters is normally a writer; here he is the one who delivers the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The job of carrying mail is a post for a man who handles correspondence.

clue.text: Regrettably, most of the salad got sent back

indicators.note: got sent back means the shortened word is read in reverse
most of means the word is used without its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner unhappily returns a nearly full salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the D from SALAD to give SALA, and 'got sent back' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of sorrow, used like unfortunately.

clue.text: Nasty wound which got Pole to grind his teeth

indicators.note: which got means the wound took the pole's letter inside it

parts.note: a nasty wound is a gash
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A man so badly hurt he grinds his teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To grit one's teeth together in anger or pain.

clue.text: Part of the hand which is held by the foot!

indicators.note: held by puts the little word is inside the foot abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for foot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A joke about a hand gripped by a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The hand clenched with fingers curled tight forms a punching shape.

clue.text: Bill which the man found a pain

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man distressed by an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous hurt is a pain.

clue.text: A fish growing medium

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish tank substrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaweed jelly used in laboratories to culture bacteria.

clue.text: It's attractive, but only when in current use

definitions.text: It's attractive, but only when in current use

parts.words: It's attractive, but only when in current use
parts.note: attractive in the magnetic sense, working only while electric current flows, not fashionable at present

explanation.definitionFit: A coil round an iron core becomes magnetic only while electricity passes through it.

clue.text: Showing compassion about a lady is right, but could be influenced by her money!

definitions.text: could be influenced by her money

indicators.note: about says the word for compassion goes round the lady and right

parts.note: showing compassion is showing mercy
Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A kind man courts a wealthy woman, perhaps for her money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing' is a link word, and Ena is just a crossword name for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mercenary is motivated chiefly by financial gain.
